alerts.title: Rising creatinine and declining eGFR on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for patients on TDF, serum creatinine and eGFR should be monitored every 12 months, and if GFR is <60 mL/min, TDF should be substituted with ABC. This patient's creatinine has risen steadily from 0.9 (2020) to 1.4 mg/dL (2026), with eGFR now 52 mL/min/1.73m²—below the 60 mL/min threshold. TDF is a known cause of chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome. Evidence for drug attribution includes the progressive decline temporally linked to 3 years of TDF therapy and proteinuria on urinalysis. Evidence against includes the absence of Fanconi-type features (no bone pain, fractures, or marked polyuria) and stable weight without oedema. Occasional ibuprofen use (2–3 times weekly) may also contribute to renal impairment and compounds the risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Substitute TDF with ABC (or AZT if ABC contraindicated) given eGFR <60. Do LFTs and RFTs. Counsel on avoiding NSAIDs including ibuprofen.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for TDF-experienced patients. This patient's latest eGFR is 52 mL/min/1.73m², which per guidelines warrants substitution of TDF. No assessment or plan was documented for this visit, meaning the significant renal decline and proteinuria have not been addressed. Additionally, no alternative regimen plan, renal referral, or medication review (including ibuprofen counselling) has been recorded.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment of declining renal function. Plan TDF substitution per guidelines, counsel on NSAID avoidance, and arrange renal evaluation for proteinuria.

alerts.title: Ibuprofen use compounding TDF renal risk
alerts.message: The patient takes ibuprofen 400 mg 2–3 times weekly for headaches. NSAIDs can reduce renal perfusion via prostaglandin inhibition, worsening renal function. Combined with TDF, which is nephrotoxic, and an eGFR already at 52 mL/min/1.73m², this compounds the risk of further renal decline. The proteinuria detected on urinalysis may reflect ongoing renal tubular injury from combined TDF and NSAID exposure.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to discontinue or minimise ibuprofen use. Consider alternative headache management such as paracetamol. Monitor renal function closely.

EFV 400 mg can be co-administered with Rifampicin-containing anti-TB treatment, with co-administration well tolerated and plasma concentrations maintained above the levels considered to be effective.
